label: gen-abund
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{gen-abund}
Let $X$ be a compact irreducible hyperk\"{a}hler manifold, 
and let $L$ be a nef line bundle on $X$.
Then $L$ is semiample.
head: environment
name: Generalized abundance for compact hyperk\"{a}hler manifolds

label: cor:finiteness
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:finiteness}
The number of
deformation classes of compact hyperk\"{a}hler manifolds, of fixed dimension, 
with $b_2\geq 5$, is finite.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $b_2\geq5$, Meyer's theorem gives 
a nonzero integral isotropic
class. A very general deformation keeping 
it of Hodge type $(1,1)$ has Picard
rank one. Thus, up to sign, it is nef, as 
there are no classes of negative
square in the Picard group. By \Cref{gen-abund}, 
this deformation admits a Lagrangian fibration. 
Then \cite[Thm.~B]{EFGMS25} gives finitely 
many deformation classes of
such manifolds in fixed dimension, 
proving the corollary.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
A real $2n$-dimensional connected submanifold $F\subset M$ is \emph{special Lagrangian} for
$(J,\omega_J,\Omega_J)$ with phase $\theta$ if $\omega_J|_F=0$ and
$\Im(e^{i\theta}\Omega_J)|_F=0$.
It is \emph{$I$-holomorphic Lagrangian} if it is an
$I$-complex submanifold and $\sigma_I|_F=0$.
head: environment

label: lem:holspc
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $(N, g, \omega, I)$ be a complex K\"{a}hler manifold and $F \subset N$ be an orientable real submanifold of dimension $2m$. Let $\mathrm{vol}_{F}$ denote the Riemannian volume form of the induced metric $g|_{F}$. Then 
  $$\bigg| \frac{\omega^{m}}{m!} \bigg|\le
  \mathrm{vol}_{F},$$
  and equality holds if and only if $F$ is a complex submanifold.
head: environment
name: Wirtinger's inequality

title: Proof
body_md:
$(1)\Rightarrow (2)$:   $\omega_{K}|_{F} = \Im(\sigma_I|_F)=0$. $(2)\Rightarrow (3)$:  trivial. $(3)\Rightarrow (1)$: The special Lagrangianity of $F$ implies that $e^{i\theta}\Omega_{J} =\pm \mathrm{vol}_{F}$; see \cite[\S I.8.1]{GHJ2003} or \cite[Cor.~III.1.11]{HB1982}. Integrating along $F$, we obtain 
\[
\mathrm{Vol}(F)=
\bigg|\int_F
\Omega_J \bigg| = \bigg|\frac{1}{n!}\int_F
(\omega_{K} + i \omega_I)^n \bigg| = \bigg| \frac{i^n}{n!} \int_{F} \omega_I^n \bigg| \leq 
\int_{F} \bigg|\frac{\omega_I^n}{n!} \bigg|
\leq \mathrm{Vol}(F),\]
by (3) and Wirtinger's inequality. Equality throughout forces the equality case in Wirtinger's inequality, i.e., $F$ is an $I$-complex submanifold. 

 In particular, $\sigma_{I}|_{F} =(\omega_{J}+i\omega_K)|_{F}=i \omega_{K}|_{F}$ is a complex (2,0)-form. The identity $\sigma_{I}(Iv, w)=i\sigma_{I}(v,w)$, with $v,w \in TF$, gives $\omega_{K}(Iv, w)=i\omega_{K}(v,w)$, but the left side is real and the right side is imaginary, so $\sigma_{I}|_{F} = \omega_{K}|_{F}=0$. We conclude that $F$ is $I$-holomorphic Lagrangian.
head: environment

label: lem:technico
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:technico}
Let $F$ be a compact special Lagrangian submanifold for
$(J,\omega_J,\Omega_J)$ such that
\[
\mathrm{PD}[F]=c\lambda^n \quad \text{ with }\lambda \in H^2(M, \mathbb Q), \quad q(\lambda)=0, \quad c\in \mathbb Q.
\]
Then, \[\int_F \alpha^n = c' q(\lambda, \alpha)^n\] for any $\alpha\in H^2(M, \mathbb C)$; here $c'\coloneqq c\,c_M\,2^n\binom{2n}{n}^{-1}$. Thus
$c \neq 0$, $q(\lambda, \sigma_{J}) \neq 0$, and $q(\lambda, \omega_J)=0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take the Fujiki's relation $\int_M (s \lambda + \alpha)^{2n} = c_M q(s \lambda + \alpha)^n=
c_M(2s q(\lambda, \alpha) +q(\alpha))^n$ and compare the coefficients of $s^n$:
\[
{2n \choose n} \int_F \alpha^n = c\,{2n \choose n} \int_M \lambda^n \alpha^n = c\,c_M\,2^n q(\lambda, \alpha)^n.
\]
In particular, $c \neq 0$ and $q(\lambda, \sigma_{J}) \neq 0$ since the special Lagrangian property entails \[|\mathrm{PD}[F] \cdot \Omega_{J}| = \bigg|\int_F \Omega_{J}\bigg|=\bigg|\int_F \frac{\sigma^n_{J}}{n!}\bigg|=|c'| \frac{|q(\lambda, \sigma_J)|^n}{n!}=\mathrm{Vol}(F)> 0.\]
Similarly, we have $0=\int_F \omega_J^n = c' q(\lambda, \omega_J)^n$.
head: environment

label: prop:PDholLag
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:PDholLag}
Let $(M, g, I, J, K)$ be a compact irreducible hyperk\"{a}hler manifold of complex dimension $2n$. Let $F$ be a compact special Lagrangian submanifold for
$(J,\omega_J,\Omega_J)$ with phase $\theta$ such that
\[
\mathrm{PD}[F]=c\lambda^n \quad \text{ with }\lambda \in H^2(M, \mathbb Q), \quad q(\lambda)=0, \quad c\in \mathbb Q.
\]
Then $F$ is $I'$-holomorphic Lagrangian with $I'\coloneqq \sin(\varphi)I + \cos(\varphi)K$ and $\varphi \coloneqq \arg q(\lambda, \sigma_{J})$. Moreover, $\lambda \in H^{1,1}(M, I')$  and $q(\lambda,\omega_{I'})>0$.
head: environment

label: eq:identity
title: Proof
body_md:
The triple $(I', J'\coloneqq J, K'\coloneqq I'J)$ is a hyperk\"{a}hler triple for $g$ with $\sigma_{J'}\coloneqq \omega_{K'}+i\omega_{I'}=e^{i \psi}\sigma_{J}$ with $\psi \coloneqq \pi/2-\varphi$. Note that $q(\lambda, \omega_{K'})=0$, because
$q(\lambda, \omega_{K'})+iq(\lambda, \omega_{I'})=q(\lambda, e^{i \psi}\sigma_{J})=e^{i \psi}e^{i\varphi}|q(\lambda, \sigma_{J})|=i|q(\lambda, \sigma_{J})|$. Since $\Im(e^{i\theta}\sigma^n_J) = \Im(e^{i(\theta -n\psi)}\sigma^n_{J'})$, $F$ is a special Lagrangian submanifold for
$(J',\omega_{J'},\sigma^n_{J'}/n!)$ with phase $\theta -n\psi$. By \Cref{lem:technico} and $q(\lambda, \omega_{K'})=0$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:identity}
\int_F (\omega_{K'}+i\omega_{I'})^n
=
c'q(\lambda, \omega_{K'}+i\omega_{I'})^n
=
c'q(\lambda, i\omega_{I'})^n
=
i^n\int_F \omega_{I'}^n.
\end{equation}
By \Cref{lem:holspc}, \eqref{eq:identity} implies that $F$ is $I'$-holomorphic Lagrangian. Finally, $\sigma_{I'} = \omega_{J} + i\omega_{K'}$
and
$q(\lambda,\omega_J)=q(\lambda,\omega_{K'})=0$.
Thus,
$q(\lambda,\sigma_{I'})=0$,
i.e.,
$\lambda\in H^{1,1}(M,I')$. The same calculation gives $q(\lambda,\omega_{I'})=|q(\lambda,\sigma_J)|>0$.
head: environment

label: rmk:profound
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:profound} The ambient isotopy type of $\mathbb T^{d}$ does not depend either on the choice of the
coordinates $(x_0, \ldots, x_d)$ or on the choice of the minimal stratum of $X_0$; see \cite[Rmk 3.7]{HM22}. Profound tori can be defined also in a neighborhood of a stratum of dimension $0$ of a semistable model, but in general its ambient isotopy class depends on the stratum, and it is independent if it is a minimal model. By \cite[Lem.~16]{dFKX17}, a neighbourhood of a stratum of dimension $0$ in $X_0$ is isomorphic to a neighbourhood of a stratum of dimension $0$ in the semistable model, so every profound torus in the dlt model is isotopic to a profound torus in the semistable model.
head: environment

label: thm:metricSYZ
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:metricSYZ} \cite{li2026, blumli2026}
Let $\pi\colon (X, H) \to \mathbb D^*$ be a polarized maximal degeneration of Calabi--Yau manifolds.  Given any
$0<\delta\ll 1$,
for sufficiently small \(t\), depending on \(\delta\), there exists a special Lagrangian  torus fibration with respect to the Calabi--Yau structure $
\left(X_t,\,\omega_{\mathrm{CY},t},\,\Omega_t\right),$ on an open subset  of \(X_t\) whose normalised Calabi--Yau measure is at least
$1-\delta$. The fiber of the fibration is isotopic to a profound torus, and the base of the fibration is an open subset of $\mathcal D(X_{0})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first part of the statement follows from \cite[Conjecture 1.1, p.~4]{li2026}. Near a minimal stratum, the fibration is a small
perturbation of the torus fibration
\[(x_1, \ldots, x_d) \mapsto \frac{1}{\log|t|}
(\log|x_1|, \ldots, \log|x_d|),\]
so the fibers are isotopic to profound tori.
head: environment

label: lem:weight
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weight}
Let $\pi\colon X\to\mathbb D^*$ be a maximal 
degeneration of compact
hyperk\"{a}hler manifolds of complex dimension $2n$, with
limit mixed Hodge
structure $(H^*_{\rm lim}, W_{\bullet}H^*_{\rm lim})$ on $H^*(X_t,\mathbb Q)$.
There exists a nonzero class $\lambda \in H^2(X_t,\mathbb Q)$, isotropic for the BBF form $q$, such that 
$$
W_0H^2_{\mathrm{lim}}=\mathbb Q \lambda,\qquad
W_0H^{2n}_{\mathrm{lim}}=\mathbb Q\lambda^n.
$$ 
The Poincar\'e dual of every profound torus lies in  $W_0H^{2n}_{\mathrm{lim}}= \mathbb Q\lambda^n$. If it is isotopic to a special Lagrangian torus,
this class is nonzero.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
After a finite base change, the monodromy operator $T_k$ on $H^k(X_t, \mathbb Q)$ is unipotent, and $T_2$ preserves $q$, i.e., $q(T_2 \alpha, T_2 \alpha')=q(\alpha, \alpha')$ with $\alpha, \alpha' \in H^2(X_t, \mathbb Q)$. The logarithmic monodromy operator $N_k = \log T_{k}$ on  $H^k(X_t, \mathbb Q)$ is nilpotent of nilpotency index  $k+1$ for even $k \leq 2n$, i.e., $N^{k}_{k} \neq 0$ but $N^{k+1}_{k} = 0$,  and $q(N_2 \alpha, \alpha')=-q(\alpha, N_2\alpha')$; see \cite[Prop.~7.14]{KLSV2018} and \cite[Lem.~2.1]{HM23}. Hence, $W_0H^2_{\mathrm{lim}}=\mathrm{Im}(N^2_2)$ is isotropic since 
$q(N^2_2 \alpha, N^2_2 \alpha')=-q(N_2\alpha, N^3_2\alpha')=0$. 
Moreover, 
$$W_0H^{2k}_{\rm lim}\simeq W_0 {\rm Sym}^k H^2_{\rm lim}\simeq {\rm Sym}^kW_0H^2_{\rm lim} \simeq \mathbb Q \lambda^k$$ for all $k\leq n$.
Indeed, we have ${\rm Sym}^k H^2_{\rm lim}\subset H^{2k}_{\rm lim}$ for $k\leq n$ by \cite[Thm.~1.5]{Ver96}. The Hodge filtration on
its orthogonal complement has level $<2k$, and  therefore the weights of this complement
are supported between $2$ and $4k-2$; see also \cite[Proof of Prop.~7.14]{KLSV2018}.

By Clemens description of maximal vanishing cycles of semistable fillings in
\cite{Clemens1969} and \cite[Thms.~3.5,~3.8]{Harder19}, the fundamental class of a profound torus $\mathbb T^{2n}$ lies in $W_{-4n}H_{2n}(X_t, \mathbb Q)$, so its Poincar\'{e} dual lies in $W_0H^{2n}_{\mathrm{lim}}$; cf.~\Cref{rmk:profound} for the comparison of semistable and dlt fillings.   
Finally, a special Lagrangian torus $F$ has
$|\int_{F}\Omega_t|>0$, so its class is nonzero.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L$ be a nef line bundle on a compact hyperk\"{a}hler manifold $M$.
If $q(L)>0$, then $M$ is projective
and $L$ is big, and the semiampleness follows from the base point free theorem. So assume that $L$ is non-trivial with $q(L)=0$.

 A {\it marking} of $M$ is an isometry from 
$H^2(M,\mathbb Z)$ to a fixed reference lattice. 
Let $\mathcal{M}$ 
denote a connected component 
of the moduli space of marked 
hyperk\"ahler manifolds containing $M$
with a given marking.
Let $\mathcal{M}_\lambda\subset \mathcal{M}$ 
be the sub-moduli space
on which a reference isotropic class $\lambda$ is the first 
Chern class $\lambda = c_1(L)$ of a nef line bundle $L$. It is connected as in \cite[Prop.~2.7]{SV2025}. So 
by \cite[Thm.~3.8]{SV2025}, it suffices to prove that $L$
is semiample on one member of $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$.

We first construct a projective maximal degeneration $\pi\colon (X, H) \to \mathbb D^*$ 
of compact hyperk\"{a}hler
manifolds, admitting a classifying
map $\mathbb{H}\to \mathcal{M}$ from the universal cover $\mathbb{H}$ of $\mathbb D^*$, and such that
$W_0 H^2_{\mathrm{lim}}=\mathbb Q\lambda$, with respect
to the marking arising from
this map. We follow \cite[\S 4]{Sold2019}. Choose an
integral vector $\mu\in \lambda^\perp$
with $q(\mu)>0$.
Define a nilpotent operator $N\in \frak{so}(H^2(M,\mathbb Z))$
by $N x \coloneqq  q(x, \mu)\lambda - q(x, \lambda)\mu.$ Fix some $v\in \{\lambda,\mu\}^\perp$ integral,
 with $q(v)>0$, and choose a line $\mathbb C z \in \mathbb{P}(v^{\perp_q}\otimes \mathbb C)$, 
 with $q(z, \lambda)=1$, $q(z, z)=0$.
Then $N^3=0$, $N^2\neq 0$. The period
mapping $\sigma_t \coloneqq {\rm exp}(\frac{\log t}{2\pi i} N)\cdot \mathbb C z$ is well-defined on
$\mathbb{H}$ for small $t$ and
induces a map to the period quotient
for $v$-quasipolarized hyperk\"ahler
manifolds. This map descends to
$\mathbb D^*$ for $\mu$ sufficiently divisible, i.e., as long as ${\rm exp}(N)$ is a monodromy operator
of the unmarked moduli space; cf.~\cite[Thm.~2.6]{Verb20} and \cite[Thm.~8.2]{BL2022}.
Hence, by global Torelli \cite{Verb13, huyglob}, we get
a degeneration $X \to \mathbb D^*$ of hyperk\"ahler manifolds.
Furthermore, a
choice of marking of $X_t$ 
for which the multivalued
period map on $\mathbb D^*$
is $t\mapsto \mathbb C[\sigma_t]$ defines
a classifying map $\mathbb{H}\to \mathcal M$ identifying
$W_0H^2_{\rm lim}$ with
the chosen isotropic ray $\mathbb Q \lambda$.


                                    
                                                 
                                            
                                            

                               
                                        
                                                                                        

The logarithmic monodromy is $N$, with 
$W_0 H^2_{\mathrm{lim}}=\mathrm{Im}(N^2)=\mathbb Q\lambda$, with respect to
the map $\mathbb{H}\to \mathcal{M}$. 
By algebraic approximation, we may ensure
that $X\to \mathbb D^*$ is an analytic restriction
of an algebraic 
family with the same 
logarithmic monodromy $N$
and very general Picard rank $1$.
Possibly after shrinking $\mathbb D^*$ and taking a finite cover, the conditions $q(v)>0$, $q(v, [\sigma_t])=0$,
and the Picard rank $1$ condition ensure that
$v$ defines a relatively ample line bundle.
So $X\to \mathbb D^*$ is projective.
After a further finite base change, 
it admits a semistable filling, and 
the hypotheses of \S\ref{metric-syz} are satisfied. The degeneration is maximal by \cite[Prop.~7.14.(ii)]{KLSV2018}.

By \Cref{thm:metricSYZ}
and \Cref{lem:weight}, 
for sufficiently small $t$, $(X_t, J, \omega_J \coloneqq
\omega_{{\rm CY},t}, \Omega_t)$ contains a special Lagrangian torus
$F$ with $\mathrm{PD}[F]=c\lambda^n$, $c \neq 0$,  isotopic to
a profound torus. 
The Ricci-flat metric on $X_t$ is hyperk\"{a}hler;
choose a compatible triple $(I,J,K)$. Its volume form
$\Omega_J=\sigma_J^n/n!$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of $\Omega_t$,
so $F$ remains special Lagrangian for $\Omega_J$. 

By \Cref{prop:PDholLag}, the manifold $X_{t}$ admits a complex structure $I'$ such that $(X_t,I')\in \mathcal{M}$, $F$ is an $I'$-holomorphic Lagrangian torus, and $\lambda \in H^{1,1}(X_t, I')$. 
So there is a
line bundle with $c_1(L)=\lambda$.
Up to a small deformation of 
$(X_t,I',L,F)$, we can
suppose that $(X_t, I')$ is non-projective with
$\mathrm{Pic}(X_t, I')_{\mathbb Q} = \mathbb Q L$; see the argument of \cite[Prop.~A.6]{EFGMS25}. 
Hence $L$ is nef and 
$(X_t,I')\in \mathcal{M}_\lambda$.
By \cite[Thm 4.1]{GLR2013}, there exists a Lagrangian fibration $f \colon (X_t, I') \to B$ with fiber $F$ and normal projective base $B$. The pullback of an ample line bundle of $B$ must be a multiple of $L$. Thus $L$ is semiample on $(X_t, I')$. As explained above, by \cite[Thm.~3.8]{SV2025},
$L$ remains semi-ample in $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$. This proves the SYZ conjecture.
